title: AdmissionPolicy
description: Defines which computed evidential states are admitted into a query-time graph projection. An admission policy is applied AFTER evidential state is computed; it does not change the state, only whether a relation in that state is admitted for traversal/return. Recommended standard policies: `strict-supported` (admit only supported), `recall-with-contested` (admit supported and contested, preserving state in results), `audit-all-registered` (return all for audit, but do not traverse unsupported/inadmissible relations unless explicitly requested).

id.description: Opaque, unique identifier for this policy.

admittedStates.description: The evidential states admitted into the projection. For traversal projections this SHOULD be a subset of {supported, refuted, contested}; admitting `unsupported` is reserved for audit-style policies, which MUST NOT drive traversal or ranking.

minimumReviewStatus.description: Pi_review: the minimum review status an evidence record must have to ground admission. The permitted values are ONLY `proposed` and `accepted`. `rejected` and `superseded` are absent by construction: they are not higher levels of review but terminal outcomes, and a policy naming one would be meaningless -- under NO policy do such records ground a relation, though they remain stored and auditable. Pi_review is therefore always a subset of {proposed, accepted}. `accepted` yields a reviewed-evidence policy; `proposed` admits unreviewed extraction as well; omitting the property takes the permissive reading. Whether unreviewed extraction may ground an answer is a deliberate deployment decision and SHOULD be declared explicitly.

includeContested.description: Convenience flag; when true, contested relations are admitted (and their state preserved in results).

includeRefuted.description: Convenience flag; when true, refuted relations are admitted (typically for audit).
